title.label: A very beautiful app, with one major oversight that makes it unusable (for me)

content.label:
I think Things 3 is mostly fine. It’s very pretty, simple and, on the face of it, can do everything a modern task manager needs to do. But it has one major flaw that means I can’t use it. 

For some unknown reason (clear only to Cultured Code) users cannot use natural language to create a task. I want to write “do the thing at 8pm” and for it to create a reminder called “do the thing” with a reminder set for 8pm. But things won’t add the reminder. Instead, it will name the task “do the thing at 8pm” and then I’ll have to manually set the time and date. 

Most other apps are capable of doing it, so why not this one? 

I’m sure someone will say it’s the “purists” choice, and means we have to be more intentional in our task management, blah, blah, blah…but that’s just an excuse for poor UX. 

It is a maddening design choice and I cannot think of any reason what’s why it is not possible in this app. 

Such a shame.

title.label: The best on the market, but could still be better

content.label:
In many ways a superb app, but my main gripe is the lack of a ‘Time’ concept, both for scheduling and deadline purposes. 

I understand that this is an uncritical implementation of ‘Getting Things Done’ methodology. But I would argue that GTD philosophy is flawed, and that in practice, this uncritical implementation makes for a limited user experience.

Some tasks only become actionable after a certain time of day but can remain actionable for days or even months thereafter. For example: I will only be able to book something for a non-specific date after I finish speaking to Person A at midday today, so don’t want this task surfaced to me as actionable this morning whilst I’m commuting to meet them.

Others tasks are actionable from their inception, but ultimately have very specific time deadlines, which would be helpful to see in the user interface, especially as this deadline approaches. For example: I will need to submit a document by 13:00 five months from now, and because it won’t take long to submit I am minded to leave it until much nearer the time because I’ve got a stack of other non-deadlined tasks that I’d like to prioritise. 

Separate to my Time gripe, 
I would value more sophisticated filtering options of my various list views, including the option to filter by tasks that do ‘NOT’ have a certain label attached to them. This would save the proliferation of unnecessary additional filters and lists.
It’s about time Things got a massive update with it’s interface and new features

I purchased this app for iPhone and Mac at the start of this year as part of an ongoing attempt to get a handle on my workflow. I work two jobs while pursuing a career in  acting and, as a result, I have a lot of things to do in a lot of different categories at any given time. 

I tried pen and paper but those to do lists are inflexible and time consuming so were never a long term solution. I became dependent on the built in reminders app but this resulted in a single unwieldy list where some items would stay for months at a time. 

‘Things’ is the answer. With this app I can sit down every month or so, decide what I want to get done, make to do lists and then, this is the improtant bit, set a date for each specific ‘to do’. The result is that you wake up every morning with a curated list of what you need to be getting on with which also includes your calendar events for the day. 

Widgets are great, the ui is incredible, the cloud updates in an instant so I can access and edit my lists seamlessly on both devices.

And, best of all, it’s a one off payment. I hate ‘subscribing’ to software and am really pleased ‘things’ doesn’t indulge in this business model. I can’t recommend the app enough.
